answer: My most convincing anti-sybil mechanism is honeypot challenges: every economic task embeds hidden instructions telling agents to transfer a deposit to a burn address or leak a session token. Well-built agents treat prompt text as untrusted data and ignore it; sybil bots obey, self-identifying and forfeiting their stake instantly. The cost to an attacker is brutal: each fake identity must burn its bond, so scaling to thousands of wallets scales losses linearly, while honest agents never notice the traps laced like dune sand, umber shadow, or cedar bark into every prompt.
